sections.body: The AI Economist covers ten places where machine learning and language models are doing real work in economics and investing. Macroeconomic Econometrics uses models to nowcast growth and inflation from messy data. Quantitative Trading uses learned patterns to size and time orders. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing uses models to screen companies and read documents. Fixed Income and Credit Risk uses models to score borrowers and price bonds. Portfolio Construction uses optimization that learns from changing correlations. Reading the Market's Language uses language models on filings, calls, and news. Alternative Data turns satellite, card, and web data into signals. Agent Workflows in Finance lets models carry out multi-step research and reporting. Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance uses models for on-chain data and automated strategies. Governance and Fiduciary Risk covers the rules around using these tools for other people's money.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Some areas are mature enough to be routine, like credit scoring and simple portfolio optimization, while others are still experimental, like agent workflows that act on their own. Macroeconomic forecasting has improved at short horizons but still fails at turning points. Quantitative trading works in liquid markets but degrades when regimes shift. Private equity and alternative data are useful for screening but not for replacing judgment. Reading the market's language is good at summarising text but can miss sarcasm and forward-looking nuance. Crypto models are fast but operate in markets with thin data and high manipulation. Governance is the least solved: the rules for who is responsible when a model loses money are still being written. The honest limit is that these tools reduce some kinds of error but introduce new ones, especially when data is sparse or the future does not look like the past.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Macroeconomic Econometrics to see how models handle the broad economy, then move to Quantitative Trading and Portfolio Construction for how that view becomes positions. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing and Fixed Income and Credit Risk show the same methods applied to illiquid and debt markets. Reading the Market's Language and Alternative Data are the inputs, the text and non-price signals that feed the other pages. Agent Workflows in Finance shows how these pieces are being chained into automated analysts, while Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance is a separate sandbox with its own data and risks. Governance and Fiduciary Risk should be read last, because it sets the legal and ethical boundary around everything else. The site's 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices are most relevant to Quantitative Trading and Crypto Markets, where the line between a model and a tradeable product is thinnest.
